rationale: Review the retained observer-branch experiment and consolidate it with the follower, control, and timeout receipts. The observer comparison is violated: observer 4 admitted context A, voter 3's later context B was confirmed first, and the reply addressed to observer 4 carried B. This measures the leader-side observer scope of the same cause; it does not exercise the observer's NodeHost consumer or completion, which remain source-only and unmeasured.

knowledge.statement: In the leader-side observer case, observer 4 admitted ReadIndex context {101,1002}; voter 3's later context {202,2003} was confirmed first; the ReadIndex reply addressed to observer 4 carried {202,2003} with log index 1, and the leader's pending ReadIndex queue was empty.
knowledge.conditions: Real internal/raft handlers with voting members {1,2,3} and a test-only observer map entry for node 4; a committed current-term no-op; observer-originated ReadIndex context A and voter-originated later context B queued; voter 3's heartbeat response for B delivered first; no NodeHost observer forwarding or pending-read consumer in this leader-side experiment.

interpretations.rationale: The current conclusion remains a bounded liveness and client-contract defect for remote ReadIndex requests when a later queued context is confirmed first. The follower receipt admits node 2's context {101,1002} and node 3's context {202,2003}; event 2 replies to node 2 with node 3's context and log index 4; event 3 leaves node 2's original batch at index zero after the real ready index 4 was applied; event 4 shows the later context-101 confirmation produces no context-correct reply and no completion. The source cause remains handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation using the confirming heartbeat's Hint/HintHigh instead of the queued request's s.ctx, while confirm deletes the earlier queue entry and pendingReadIndex.addReady requires an exact SystemCtx key. The sequential control confirms the same consumer path with node 2's admitted context first: its reply carries that context and completion is 1 with batch index 4. The logical-deadline case keeps the later-first ordering: its event 1 records original_batch_index zero, no completion before the 50-tick deadline, RequestTimeout at advanced tick 51, and the stale batch absent after GC. The observer leader-side experiment admits observer 4's context A, queues voter 3's later context B, confirms B first, and observes the reply addressed to observer 4 carrying B with log index 1; this measures the same leader-side substitution for an observer source. Together the receipts distinguish a context-association defect from a general consumer or harness failure, measure the bounded follower endpoint, and extend the leader-side reply defect to observer sources. The main reply's log index is a later committed index, so no stale-read value or safety violation is established. The main request remains uncompleted after a valid applied index until the measured logical timeout; the observer's local pending-read consumer and completion were not measured.

knowledge.assertion: The confirming context returns earlier queued requests while preserving each request's own SystemCtx.
Remote replies are tagged with the confirming heartbeat context instead of the queued request's context.
A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.
The exercised later-confirmation ordering produced a mismatched reply context and left the earlier read batch unready after the ready index was applied.
The sequential-confirmation control completed when the admitted context was confirmed first.
The logical-deadline case returned RequestTimeout at tick 51 and removed the stale batch.
Observer-originated ReadIndex requests enter the same leader queue and pending-read response path.
The observer leader-side reply carried the later confirming context rather than the observer's admitted context.

counterevidence: The source path that constructs the remote reply uses m.Hint and m.HintHigh; no re-tagging occurs between that send and node 2's consumer in the main probe.
The main reply's log index was 4 and the ready index was 4, so neither the main nor timeout execution shows a stale committed index or stale application state.
The late context-101 confirmation produced zero context-correct replies and completion remained zero.
The sequential control completed with the admitted context, so the main failure is not a general inability of the harness or pending-read consumer to complete.
The timeout receipt shows a client timeout and cleanup, not a successful stale read; it measures the bounded endpoint without establishing a safety violation.
The observer experiment measures only the leader-side reply context; it does not execute the observer's local forwarding or pending-read completion.
limitations: The ILogDB is test-only and in-memory; disk failure, restart, snapshots, and real transport delay were not exercised.
The main test applies the returned ready index synchronously; the companion timeout receipt measures the logical deadline at tick 51, not wall-clock scheduling.

Observer-originated reads are measured only at the leader-side reply; the observer NodeHost forwarding and pending-read consumer are source-traced but not measured. Other membership layouts were not measured.
The sequential control holds only for its exercised first-context ordering; it does not establish safety or completion for all schedules.
The observed wrong reply context is a correlation defect; it is not by itself evidence that the returned read index is stale or that a wrong data value was read.
interpretations.joint_history: The follower, control, and timeout receipts come from the same three-peer in-memory harness family; the observer receipt uses a focused internal Raft leader with voters {1,2,3} and observer 4. All four experiments are under the same ReadIndex investigation and exercise the same leader-side confirmation path. The follower and observer cases both queue an earlier remote context before a later voter context and confirm the later one first; the control confirms the admitted context first; the timeout repeats the later-first ordering and advances the pending-read logical clock. The observer case does not include the observer's local consumer, so its result is limited to the leader-side reply.
